newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-U.S., WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS IN JEOPARDY FOR JOHNSON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-U.S., WORLD CHAMPIONSHIPS IN JEOPARDY FOR JOHNSON.

text.p: World 200-meter record-holder Michael Johnson's appearances in the U.S. and world championships are in jeopardy because of an injury the double Olympic champion suffered in Sunday's race with Canadian Donovan Bailey.

"He has a severe pull in his left quadricep," a spokeswoman for Brad Hunt, Johnson's agent, quoted Hunt as saying on Monday. "It will be at least a week before he can train. The national championships are in jeopardy."

If Johnson cannot compete in the U.S. championships, which begin June 11 in Indianapolis, he would not be eligible for the August world championships in Athens, U.S. athletics spokesman Pete Cava said.
"He must finish in the top three to qualify for an individual event in the world championships," Cava said.
Johnson failed to finish his 150-meter match race with Bailey in Toronto's SkyDome on Sunday, saying he felt what he thought was a cramp in his left leg.
He has returned to his Dallas hometown and is under a doctor's supervision, the spokeswoman said.
